title: Daytona USA
shortDescription: Sega AM2's legendary stock-car arcade racing landmark, introducing texture-mapped 60 FPS 3D polygons on the Model 2 arcade hardware.
historicalSignificance: One of the highest-grossing arcade games in history, setting the worldwide gold standard for 3D arcade driving with its blazing 60 FPS texture mapping, 8-player cabinet linking, and iconic 'Let's Go Away' vocal music by Takenobu Mitsuyoshi.

editorialContent.overview: Directed by Toshihiro Nagoshi under supervisor Yu Suzuki, Daytona USA brought high-speed NASCAR-inspired stock car drifting to arcades worldwide on Sega's groundbreaking Model 2 arcade board.
editorialContent.gameplay: Blistering drift mechanics around Three-Seven Speedway, Dinosaur Canyon, and Seaside Street Galaxy, navigating packs of 40 simultaneous stock cars at 200 MPH with force-feedback steering.
editorialContent.technicalInnovation: The first arcade game to feature hardware texture filtering and real-time lighting on 3D polygons at a locked 60 frames per second, handling 300,000 polygons per second.
editorialContent.culturalImpact: A cornerstone of 1990s arcade culture whose infectious vocal soundtrack and linked multiplayer cabinets remain beloved worldwide.
editorialContent.preservationNotes: Preserved on Sega Model 2 arcade boards, ported to Saturn and PC, and remastered for modern HD consoles.

verifiedFactualData.sales: Over $1 billion in arcade gross; one of the highest-earning coin-op titles ever
awards: Inducted into World Video Game Hall of Fame

technicalSpecs.engine: Sega Model 2 Hardware (Intel i960 @ 25 MHz + Fujitsu DSPs)
technicalSpecs.soundChip: Sega MultiPCM 28-channel audio with Mitsuyoshi vocals
technicalSpecs.mediaFormat: Arcade PCB with Force Feedback Steering
